messages:
anne_support: FYI — BrightAtlas (acct BA-789) says their mid-cycle downgrade credit is split and customer still sees an outstanding balance. Ticket #12345. I pulled the invoices and payments but need billing/eng help.

mike_finance: Can you paste the invoice ids and the credit/refund traces? quick guess: proration created a credit note + system attempted a card refund fallback, ended up as two separate settlements.

anne_support: Sure — here's what I found. INV: INV-2026-789 (EUR), CN: CN-2026-0045 applied to INV-2026-789 for EUR 1,234.50, PaymentIntent: pi_3JxExample refunded EUR 1.24. Customer expected single credit applied to PO. Logs:

```
invoice: {
  "id": "INV-2026-789",
  "amount_due": "0.00",
  "currency": "EUR",
  "lines": [ {"desc": "prod:uptime - prorated", "amount": "-1234.50"} ],
  "taxes": [{"rate": "0.20", "amount": "246.90"}]
}
payments: [{"pi": "pi_3JxExample", "status": "succeeded", "amount_refunded": "1.24", "method": "card"}]
trace_ids: ["trace-prorate-81f", "refund-req-992"]
```

sara_billing: Looking at the invoice JSON — two things jump out: 1) tax rounding on the prorated lines leaves a tiny residual (~EUR 0.10-0.20) after we create the credit note, 2) our PO flow flagged the invoice as requiring PO-approval so card refunds can't be auto-applied to that PO-backed invoice. That explains why the card refund sits as a separate refund instead of being consumed by the PO invoice.

raj_engineer: I dug into the refund workflow traces. Repro sequence: proration job creates CN, marks invoice as adjusted, then payments worker attempts refund. There's a race: if invoice state flips (po_required flag transitions) between steps, payments worker falls back to issuing a card refund instead of associating the credit to PO. Logs: 

```
[2026-06-02T09:12:33Z] job=prorate id=trace-prorate-81f created=CN-2026-0045
[2026-06-02T09:12:34Z] invoice-service set_state INV-2026-789 po_required=true
[2026-06-02T09:12:34Z] payments-worker id=refund-req-992 attempted apply_credit(INV-2026-789) -> fail(reason: invoice_locked_for_po) -> fallback refund_card(pi_3JxExample)
```

raj_engineer: I can reproduce locally with a test that toggles the po flag between steps. We should add a small transactional guarantee or single-step decision: check+apply under same DB transaction or retry.

mike_finance: From ledger side, dual settlements (credit note + card refund) created two separate accounting entries. The small rounding residual plus currency conversion caused the ledger to show EUR 1.34 unsettled. We can manually reconcile but we need a fix to avoid duplicates and to ensure refunds respect PO-association.

tom_cs_manager: Action items: 1) customer-facing: explain why this happened and offer to reconcile immediately (Anne) 2) billing: create manual adjustment/credit to clear outstanding EUR 1.34 and mark invoice settled (Sara/Mike) 3) eng: add transactional guard + test to payments/refund workflow to avoid fallback duplicates (Raj) 4) update runbook for edge-case with PO required + mid-cycle proration (Raj/Sara).

billing-bot: invoice-service: CN-2026-0046 created (manual adjustment) by sara_billing for INV-2026-789 amount EUR 1.34 — pending ledger reconciliation.

anne_support: I'll message BrightAtlas now, offer immediate settlement and confirm PO acceptance of the manual CN. Will keep thread updated.

sara_billing: I'll apply CN-2026-0046 to clear the residual and kick ledger reconcile. Will also add a note to the invoice: "manual settlement applied due to PO+refund race condition".

raj_engineer: I'll open a PR to: 1) add a DB transaction for apply_credit+state-check OR re-run apply_credit on transient invoice_lock, 2) add integration test that toggles po_required mid-flow. ETA EOD tomorrow.

mike_finance: After reconcile, I'll run a small query to find other invoices with both credit_notes and card_refunds within a 5-minute window and flag them for manual review.

anne_support: Update for customer: BrightAtlas accepted the manual CN and confirms balance shows zero. Ticket updated and customer notified. Closing loop here but leaving runbook fix work items assigned. :white_check_mark:
